Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

traditional adjective

also tradition, traditionally, time-honoured, ancestral, handed down

classical

Cic. Sen. 37: vigēbat in illā domō mōs patrius et disciplīna
Curt. 3.3.9: patrium carmen canēbant

patrius, patria, patrium

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

traditional, handed down from one’s fathers; native

Of one’s fathers, and so of one’s people: a traditional song is carmen patrium; one’s native language, patrius sermō (Cic. Fin. 1.4, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • mōre majōrum — traditionally, by ancestral custom

    phrase: mōs in the ablative · classical · Cic. Sen. 46: is sermō, quī mōre majōrum ā summō adhibētur in pōculō

    Tradition itself is mōs majōrum, the custom of the ancestors (see practice).

  • trālātīcius (trānslātīcius), trālātīcia, trālātīcium — handed down, customary; ordinary

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.8.4: hoc vērō … trālātīcium est; Phaedr. 5.7.24: mōre trānslātīciō (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. traditional

    Of edicts and practices passed on from one holder to the next: traditional, and therefore nothing remarkable.

  • avītus, avīta, avītum — ancestral, of one’s grandfathers

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 34: bona paterna et avīta (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. traditional: ancestral, time-honoured · Declension on Wiktionary

    For what is so old that it is held in reverence (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • metuēbant servī, verēbantur līberī, cārum omnēs habēbant; vigēbat in illā domō mōs patrius et disciplīna

    the slaves feared him, the children revered him, all held him dear; in that house the ways of the fathers and the old discipline were strongCic. Sen. 37

  • mē vērō et magisteria dēlectant ā majōribus īnstitūta et is sermō, quī mōre majōrum ā summō adhibētur in pōculō

    for my part I enjoy the presiding at feasts that our ancestors established, and the talk over the cup that, by ancestral custom, the head of the table beginsCic. Sen. 46

  • Magī proximī patrium carmen canēbant

    next came the Magi, singing their traditional hymnCurt. 3.3.9

See also practice, grandfather.
